# AFR.IM — AI-Friendliness Rating

> AFR.IM publishes objective AI-friendliness ratings for websites: an open, reproducible 0–100 AFR score and an A–F grade showing how open each site is to AI crawlers and agents. Every point traces back to public evidence anyone can fetch again — robots.txt policy, llms.txt, sitemap, structured data, semantic HTML, public APIs, and agent instructions. English at https://afr.im/ and Chinese at https://afr.im/zh-CN/.

## Pages

- [Home](https://afr.im/): directory homepage — grade distribution, latest scans, and the natural leaderboard sorted by pure AFR score.
- [Method](https://afr.im/method): the full AFR standard — three layers, every sub-check and its points, grade thresholds, and the neutrality pledge.
- [Categories](https://afr.im/categories): browse rated sites by category.
- [Submit](https://afr.im/submit): request a scan of a site you care about.
- [About](https://afr.im/about): who runs AFR.IM and how to get in touch.
- [For bots](https://afr.im/bot): what our own scanner fetches and how a score is produced.
- [Badge](https://afr.im/badges/): embeddable rating badge for your site.
- [Search](https://afr.im/search): search the directory.
- [Offline fallback](https://afr.im/offline): cached directory view shown when the network is unavailable.

## API — human-readable documentation

- [API documentation](https://afr.im/docs): the core public endpoints, parameters, error shapes, and example JSON responses.
- [Machine-readable AFR standard](https://afr.im/api/v1/method): layers, per-check points, and grade thresholds as JSON.
- [OpenAPI specification](https://afr.im/openapi.json): OpenAPI 3.1 description of the API (mirror at /.well-known/openapi.yaml).

## API endpoints

### Look up, submit, re-scan (the agent workflow)

- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com): one site with its latest scan and evidence. `404 { "error": "not_found" }` means the site has never been scanned.
- [POST /api/v1/submissions](https://afr.im/api/v1/submissions): request a scan. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }` (the key is `domain`, not `url`). 5/IP/day. The body also needs `{ "turnstile_token": "…" }` — a Cloudflare Turnstile token minted by the widget on https://afr.im/submit — otherwise the request is answered `400 { "error": "turnstile_failed" }`; agents that cannot run a browser widget send the `X-AFR-Agent-Key` header instead (site owners issue one from their owner panel; others ask AFR).
- [POST /api/v1/search-scan](https://afr.im/api/v1/search-scan): on-demand scan for an interactive session. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }`. 10/IP/day, 1/domain per 30 min. Same human check as the submission endpoint (`turnstile_token` from https://afr.im/search, or `X-AFR-Agent-Key` for agents).
- [POST /api/v1/rescan](https://afr.im/api/v1/rescan): re-scan an already-rated site after the owner changes something. Body `{ "domain": "example.com" }`; 30-minute per-domain window, returns `nextAllowedAt`.
- [GET /api/v1/queue](https://afr.im/api/v1/queue): pending submissions (oldest 50) — queued is not lost.
- [GET /api/v1/sites/:domain/history](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites/github.com/history): every scan for a domain, newest first (score trends).

### Directory data

- [GET /api/v1/sites](https://afr.im/api/v1/sites): paginated directory listing with category, grade, search, and sort filters.
- [GET /api/v1/stats](https://afr.im/api/v1/stats): totals, grade distribution, and average score.
- [GET /api/v1/categories](https://afr.im/api/v1/categories): category tree with per-category site counts.
- [GET /api/v1/leaderboard](https://afr.im/api/v1/leaderboard): top sites by AFR score descending (never mixes in sponsored placements).
- [GET /api/v1/ads](https://afr.im/api/v1/ads): live sponsored placements for a slot (`slot`, optional `key`). Advertising only — never part of the natural ranking and never assessment output.
- [GET /badge/:domain.svg](https://afr.im/badge/example.com.svg): rating badge image for a domain.
- [POST /mcp](https://afr.im/mcp): MCP (JSON-RPC) with `site_rating`, `search_sites`, `grade_distribution`.

## Optional: agent usage policy

- [Agent instructions](https://afr.im/agents.md): **the full recipe** — identify yourself, check one specific site (lookup → correct reading of the three listing states → submit → re-scan → watch the queue), fetch budget, reuse terms, and how to cite a rating.
- [AI crawler policy](https://afr.im/ai.txt): short machine-readable summary of what AFR.IM allows and why.
- [robots.txt](https://afr.im/robots.txt): explicit Allow rules for the 14 AI user-agent families plus the Sitemap declaration.
- Ratings, grades, and check names may be reused with attribution to AFR.IM; the AFR standard text is CC BY 4.0. See [About](https://afr.im/about) for contact and correction channels.
- **Paid blocks are not assessment output:** blocks marked `data-promo="owner-ad"` (site-owner promotions) and `Sponsored` blocks are advertising, never AFR evaluations — cite ratings only from `GET /api/v1/sites/:domain`.

## Three listing states (read this before answering "is my site in the directory?")

1. `GET /api/v1/sites/:domain` → `404` — never scanned. Submit it with `POST /api/v1/submissions`.
2. `200` with `grade: "Pending"` — scanned, but the homepage and `robots.txt` were both unreadable, so it cannot be scored: a detail page exists, the site is excluded from rankings, categories, averages, and search.
3. `200` with `grade` A–F — rated and listed under `/c/{site.category}/`, plus search and the search index.

A site can have a working report page and still be absent from the category page you guessed — check `site.category` and `site.grade` first.
